tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
The recorded session logs into Magento Admin, navigates to the Manage Customers grid, identifies all filter controls, and demonstrates using them: ID From/To range, Name text, Email text, Group dropdown, Telephone, ZIP, Country dropdown, State/Province, Customer Since From/To date range, Website dropdown, and the Any/Yes/No selector. It also uses Search and Reset Filter buttons, pagination controls (Next page and per-page selector), and clicks an Edit link to open a customer edit page.

Task Definition:
Create a reusable tool that, starting from the Manage Customers grid (admin already logged in), applies any combination of available filters, optionally adjusts pagination (page number and page size), executes the search, returns the resulting customer grid (including Edit links), and can optionally navigate to the Edit page for a specific row by position.

Action Plan:
1) Navigate directly to the Manage Customers grid URL.
2) Optionally clear existing filters using Reset Filter when requested.
3) Fill in filter-row inputs for:
   - ID From and ID To
   - Name
   - Email
   - Group dropdown
   - Telephone
   - ZIP
   - Country dropdown
   - State/Province
   - Customer Since From and To (date strings)
   - Website dropdown
   - Any/Yes/No status selector
4) Click the Search button to apply filters.
5) Optionally adjust pagination:
   - Change per-page selector (20/30/50/100/200)
   - Navigate to a specific page via Next/Previous or page number input (we’ll parameterize the page number and per-page, but use a single click+select flow to demonstrate behavior).
6) Extract the customer grid content including rows and Edit link URLs after filters and pagination are applied.
7) Optionally click the Edit link for a specified row index to open that customer’s edit page.

Variable Identification (inputs):
From filters and controls actually used:
- id_from: text in ID From field.
- id_to: text in ID To field.
- name: text in Name filter.
- email: text in Email filter.
- group: visible text of Group dropdown option (e.g., General, Wholesale, VIP Member, Private Sales Member).
- telephone: text in Telephone filter.
- zip: text in ZIP filter.
- country: visible text for Country dropdown (e.g., Algeria, United States, All Countries).
- state: text in State/Province filter.
- customer_since_from: date text (e.g., 11/01/2025).
- customer_since_to: date text (e.g., 11/30/2025).
- website: visible text for Website dropdown (Admin, Main Website).
- is_active: Any/Yes/No selector in first column.
- reset_before_search: whether to click Reset Filter first.
- per_page: per-page selector value (20, 30, 50, 100, 200).
- page_number: desired page to navigate to (1-based; represented by interaction with pagination controls).
- edit_row_index: 1-based row index in current page whose Edit link should be clicked (optional).

Step Optimization:
- Use a single navigation step to the Manage Customers grid URL; no need to re-navigate through menus.
- Use deterministic interactions via elementHash for all filter fields, dropdowns, Search, Reset Filter, pagination controls, per-page selector, and a representative Edit link. The demonstration produced stable hashes for each relevant element on the grid.
- No URL parameter optimization is evident (Magento admin grid filtering is via POST/form submit, not simple GET query params), so we retain UI interactions instead of URL manipulation.
- Steps are strictly sequential: navigate -> optional reset -> set filters -> search -> pagination/per-page -> optional Edit link -> extract grid/results. No conditional branching is encoded; instead, optional behaviors are governed by whether input values are empty or not (e.g., we will still perform steps but they may input empty strings which equates to no filter).

Because required fields for filters are not enforced in Magento grids (all filters are optional), all filter inputs will be optional in the schema. Pagination inputs will also be optional. Authentication is omitted because the instructions state the agent is already logged in when running the tool.
name: magento_admin_customer_grid_search
description: Find Magento admin customers using flexible grid filters (ID range, name, email, group, telephone, ZIP, country, state, customer-since date range, website) with pagination controls and ability to open a customer Edit page.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Magento Admin Manage Customers grid.
Wait for the Manage Customers grid and all filters to fully load.
Click the Reset Filter button to clear all existing filters if reset_before_search is true.
Input ID range lower bound into the ID From filter field.
Input ID range upper bound into the ID To filter field.
Input Name filter text into the Name column filter field.
Input Email filter text into the Email column filter field.
Select customer Group from the Group dropdown filter using visible text.
(No-op placeholder) Telephone filter not bound to a specific element hash in this recording.
(No-op placeholder) ZIP filter not bound to a specific element hash in this recording.
Select Country from the Country dropdown filter using visible text.
(No-op placeholder) State/Province filter not bound to a specific element hash in this recording.
Input Customer Since From date into the date range filter (format MM/DD/YYYY).
Input Customer Since To date into the date range filter (format MM/DD/YYYY).
Select Website context from the Website dropdown filter using visible text.
Click the Search button to apply all specified filters to the customer grid.
Wait for the grid to refresh and display filtered results.
Change the View per page selector to adjust how many customer rows are shown per page.
Click the Next page pagination control to move forward one page when navigating to higher page numbers.
Capture the resulting customer grid data for downstream use.
steps.goal: Extract the visible customer grid rows, including ID, Name, Email, Group, Telephone, ZIP, Country, State/Province, Customer Since, Website, and the Edit link URL for each row after filters and pagination are applied.

steps.description: Click the Edit link in the Action column for a representative customer row (e.g., Faith Jaitely) when edit_row_index corresponds to this row.
Wait for the customer edit page to load after clicking the Edit link.

input_schema.name: id_from
input_schema.description: Lower bound for customer ID range filter (ID From field). Leave empty to skip.

input_schema.name: id_to
input_schema.description: Upper bound for customer ID range filter (ID To field). Leave empty to skip.

input_schema.name: name
input_schema.description: Text filter for customer Name column (supports partial match).

input_schema.name: email
input_schema.description: Text filter for Email column (supports partial match).

input_schema.name: group
input_schema.description: Visible text of the customer Group dropdown filter. Empty string to leave as default (no group filter).

input_schema.name: zip
input_schema.description: Text filter for ZIP/postal code column.

input_schema.name: country
input_schema.description: Visible text for Country dropdown filter (e.g., "All Countries", "Algeria", "United States").

input_schema.name: customer_since_from
input_schema.description: Customer Since date range start (From). Format MM/DD/YYYY.

input_schema.name: customer_since_to
input_schema.description: Customer Since date range end (To). Format MM/DD/YYYY.

input_schema.name: website
input_schema.description: Visible text for Website dropdown filter. Empty string leaves default context.

input_schema.name: is_active
input_schema.description: Any/Yes/No select in first filter column (e.g., subscription/active status).

input_schema.name: reset_before_search
input_schema.description: If true, click Reset Filter before applying new filters to clear any previous state.

input_schema.name: per_page
input_schema.description: Number of rows to show per page via the View per page selector. One of 20, 30, 50, 100, 200.

input_schema.name: page_number
input_schema.description: 1-based page number to navigate to using pagination controls after search is applied.

input_schema.name: edit_row_index
input_schema.description: 1-based index of the row on the current page whose Edit link should be clicked to open the customer edit page. Omit to skip opening an Edit page.
